message.content: {"caption":"Traditional generalist-agent design contrasted with Alita’s MCP-based capability-building approach.","description":"A two-tier comparison diagram, separated by a horizontal dashed line. In the upper tier, a blue rounded box labeled “Traditional Generalist Agents” sits beside a cloud-shaped “Manager Agent,” illustrated with a person and documents. Six labeled components surround it: “Url Text Extractor” (URL document icon), “Image Captioner” (image icon), “Relevant Patch Zoomer” (magnifier over an image), “Web Agent” (browser icon), “Other Agents” (group of people), and “Path Generalist Classifier” (person and branching-path icon), plus “Youtube Caption Crawler” (video and document icon). Each component is linked to the Manager Agent by a colored two-headed arrow. To the right, a gears-and-hand icon labeled “Large-scale Manual Engineering” points via a gray right-facing arrow to a blue box listing “Incomplete Coverage,” “Limited Creativity & Flexibility,” and “Mismatch.” In the lower tier, a yellow rounded box labeled “Alita (Ours)” is followed by a browser-icon “Web Agent” and a cloud-shaped “Manager Agent,” connected by a blue two-headed arrow. The Manager Agent connects rightward through a gray arrow labeled “MCP Creation” to an “MCP Box,” and a purple left-pointing arrow labeled “Self Evolving” returns from the MCP Box toward the Manager Agent. To their right, “Minimal Predefinition” appears above a green downward arrow and gear icon; “Maximal Self-Evolution” appears below, beside a red upward arrow and a small person-like idea/evolution icon. A gray right-facing arrow leads to a yellow box listing “Scalable Dynamic Capability,” “Enhanced Creativity & Flexibility,” and “Cross-ecosystem Compatibility.”","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
